correctness.rationale: With X=T_Lambda T_{Gamma-Omega}^*, duality is exactly X=0, while the published orthogonality sum equals (I-S^{-1})X. Thus the criterion is equivalent to range(X) lying in ker(S-I). If this eigenspace is zero, injectivity gives duality. Conversely, when it is nonzero, the bounded right inverse T_Lambda^* S^{-1} realizes any nonzero operator into that eigenspace as a Bessel-family defect, proving sharp necessity. In the concrete C^2 example, the frame operator is diag(1,2), the orthogonality operator is exactly zero and the reconstruction operator is diag(2,1), so the candidate is not a dual.

evidence: These sources characterize duals or approximate duals by different mixed-operator conditions and do not justify invertibility of I-S^{-1}.

evidence: The source itself obtains (I-S^{-1})X=0 but then makes the invalid inference that I-S^{-1} is invertible.
Injectivity, not bounded invertibility, is sufficient for X=0.

final_claim: For the orthogonality criterion in Rajeswari–George Theorem 3.1, the mixed duality defect is detected only modulo the 1-eigenspace of the frame operator; the criterion characterizes every Bessel candidate as a dual exactly when 1 is not an eigenvalue, and a two-dimensional non-Parseval frame gives an explicit failure otherwise.
limitations: The result corrects only the stated orthogonality converse and does not re-audit every later theorem in the source paper.
